note: Generated by apps/core-java/tools/make-sandbox-vectors.mjs from packages/attest-rules/src/{samples,scenarios}.ts and apps/core/src/http/sandbox.ts. The evaluation sandbox's starting documents and its catalogue. Synthetic data: no payment, no institution.

settlement.purpose: Import payment for goods under INV-2026-001

scenarios.title: Normal trade payment
scenarios.teaches: All six sources agree under the policy. Note that the verdict still asks for manual review: the data is synthetic and the keys are demonstration keys, so issuer identity and business finality cannot be satisfied.

scenarios.title: Amount mismatch
scenarios.teaches: The chain transfer is 2,000 short of the instructed amount against a zero tolerance. The finding names the field, the expected value, the actual value and the tolerance it exceeded — "amounts do not match" would not be actionable.

scenarios.title: Payout signature broken
scenarios.teaches: The digest and the chain data still verify; only the provider signature fails. Integrity passing while the issuer fails is precisely the combination a single green tick would hide.

scenarios.title: Invoice missing
scenarios.teaches: The invoice is cited by number but not supplied. The result is INCOMPLETE, not INVALID — missing evidence calls for a request, forged evidence calls for escalation, and conflating them sends the reviewer down the wrong path.

scenarios.title: Split payment
scenarios.teaches: Forty per cent then sixty per cent. Whether this reconciles depends entirely on whether the policy permits aggregation — the engine does not decide that, the policy does, and the policy version is recorded in the result either way.

scenarios.title: Duplicate submission
scenarios.teaches: The same payout receipt, submitted twice. Nothing about the document is wrong — the digest matches and the signature verifies, because it is the receipt the provider signed. Integrity and issuer both pass and the payment still must not be released. This is the case that proves "the document is genuine" and "the transaction is approved" are two different questions.

tampers.label: Change an amount
tampers.asks: If someone edits a figure after approval, is it caught, and does the result say which figure?

tampers.label: Corrupt a signature
tampers.asks: If an issuer seal is forged, does integrity still pass — and is the failure attributed to the issuer rather than the document?

tampers.label: Remove a required document
tampers.asks: Is a missing document reported as missing rather than as invalid? The two call for different work.

tampers.label: Replace the document behind a digest
tampers.asks: If the file is swapped but the paperwork is left alone, which link breaks?

tampers.label: Submit the same payout twice
tampers.asks: Everything verifies and the payment must still be stopped. Does the result distinguish a genuine document from an approved transaction?
